title: Welcome to Landslide Atlas
bullets: Explore source-linked observations
Create reproducible research figures
Understand the limits before drawing conclusions
sentences: Welcome to Landslide Atlas, an open research workspace for exploring landslide reports in India.
This short guide explains how to select a region, inspect evidence, export figures, and begin a reproducible research experiment.
The dashboard is an inventory explorer, not an operational warning system or a validated national susceptibility model.

title: Choose a state and district
bullets: Choose a state or union territory
Select a district, year range and reported trigger
Read the model-availability message
sentences: In the Explore section, choose a state or union territory, then a district.
Use the event year and reported trigger filters to narrow the observation record. Decide whether to include reports without a usable date.
Read the model availability message. The exploratory Raigad pilot covers only part of that district; selecting another region does not create a trained model there.

title: Read the map carefully
bullets: Points represent reported locations
Grid shading counts reports in each cell
An empty area may simply lack reporting
sentences: Map points represent reported locations. Select a point or inspect a table entry to review its source, date, and location accuracy.
The alternative grid view counts reports in each cell. A darker cell indicates more reports, not a higher estimated failure probability.
Missing reports do not prove that an area is safe. Administrative boundaries also have documented source dates and naming limitations.

title: Export figures with provenance
bullets: Explore years, triggers, geography and completeness
Export charts or maps as SVG and PNG
Save the filtered data and reproduction manifest
sentences: The figures summarize dated reports, reported triggers, reporting geography, and the availability of selected evidence fields.
Compare these as patterns in the observation record. Raw counts do not account for surveyed area, exposure, or reporting effort.
Export a map or chart as S V G or P N G. Save the filtered C S V or Geo J S O N and the reproduction manifest so another researcher can identify the sources and filters.

title: Add observations and share a project
bullets: Supply coordinates, source and permission details
Add notes after reviewing the evidence
Export project JSON for collaborators to import
sentences: The Add observations section accepts a location and supporting source details. Record the source and reuse permission, and check the coordinates and date.
Your observations and notes remain in this browser. They are not automatically uploaded to a shared database or verified as official records.
Use Save project J S O N to back up the session and share it with collaborators, who can import that project into their own browser.

title: Run the GitHub research demonstration
bullets: Open the landslide-segmentation research module
Run the sample demonstration in GitHub Actions
Download the preview and verification report
sentences: The linked GitHub research module provides dataset sources, paper P D F links, preparation code, and an evaluation plan.
Open its research sample demonstration under Actions, then select Run workflow. Scholars without write access can fork the repository and run it in their fork.
The demonstration checks two Landslide for Sense training examples and produces an image and verification report. It prepares data; it does not train a deep learning model.

title: Understand the training example
bullets: Left: satellite RGB display
Middle: supplied binary landslide annotation
Right: supplied slope channel
sentences: The example image contains three panels: satellite imagery on the left, a supplied binary landslide annotation in the middle, and the provided slope channel on the right.
White pixels in the annotation mark mapped landslide areas in this training sample. They are not predictions made by our software.
This benchmark example is not a Maharashtra map. Cite the original Landslide for Sense dataset and preserve its attribution when reusing the example.

title: Plan the next Maharashtra study
tag: 07 / Build evidence for a defensible claim
bullets: Obtain dated local inventories and independent labels
Separate events and regions during evaluation
Use pre-event inputs for prospective prediction
sentences: For a Maharashtra study, obtain a dated local inventory and independently checked landslide boundaries, then align the satellite images and terrain inputs.
Start with a published baseline, document the data split, and keep independent events or regions for evaluation. Report errors and uncertainty as well as aggregate scores.

To claim future susceptibility or early warning, use only information available before the event and define the prediction period. The current research module is a starting point for that work, not a completed validation.
